chose: mass rename reconciliation reuses lint-sinks's count-conserving matched-disappearance shape, with the move-invariant address = family + unit + EXACT value, one reconciler for ALL dimension families
over: a type-level obligation forcing every baseline family to declare a rename policy (forgives-moves | immune-by-key | rename-is-signal) — measured, not needed: the H1-rename and measure-key-rename repros both produce the same lie shape ('gained parts nobody named' beside an unchanged total), and families with closed key sets (deps|*, files|total, symbols|total) are vacuously unaffected, so per-family semantics buy nothing but declaration surface

fuzzy/tolerance value matching so a renamed-AND-grown key inherits the old pin and fails only on the delta — rejected because pairing without value equality lets a genuinely new component pass whenever any same-family pin of matching size vanished; growth would be laundered through renames, which is the conservation property inverted
because: conservation is the honesty property: relocation changes WHERE pinned mass lives, duplication/growth changes HOW MUCH unpinned surface exists; exact-value matching is precisely 'the mass is conserved', and the renamed-and-grown case fails closed with the vanished candidate named in the report (3 → 5) so the reader sees the likely story without the gate guessing

chose: the rename block prints in mass's own words ('RENAMED — the same pinned mass under a new name, not growth', 'N units conserved') rather than reusing sinks' MOVED vocabulary
over: reporting renames as MOVED like lint-sinks — a sink site is DISCOVERED and relocates with its file; a mass dimension's name is DECLARED (spec H1, measure config key), so the honest verb is rename, even though the reconciler mechanics are identical
because: the report is the part a human reads; the asymmetry declared-vs-discovered survives contact only in the vocabulary, not in the matching semantics
